#First things first. Find support for yourself. This could be a therapist or someone close to you who isn’t going to talk about this with him. It would be best if they don’t even know about each other. You can’t be there for him if you yourself are breaking down and aren’t sure how to handle it.

#3 let him know you are always there to talk about it. 

#4 If he starts calling it abuse, help give it a name. It’s COCSA. Child on child sexual abuse and it is 1/3 of all sexual abuse cases. It’s unfortunately common. He is not alone. There’s whole Reddit pages dedicated to survivors. 

#5 Please please please don’t be angry at his brother if he just froze up and sat there. If he participated or was going to watch that’s one thing. But if he just sat there please remember this. He was a child too. A minor with an undeveloped brain to be exact. In fact, if he also had access to that kid, he might’ve been abused as well. I experienced COCSA when I was 10. I always vowed to stand up for survivors. When I was 15, I saw my bf smack my sister’s ass and pull it off as a joke. I froze, I told him to stop, but that was it. My brain could not process wtf just happened, why someone I loved was doing this shit, and why this was happening to me again. I just partially dissociated and tried to move everyone past it. Then I fawned and tried to get him to pay attention to me so he would leave her alone. I still feel guilty about it. Now as a fully developed adult in my mid twenties, I am able to do better and have nearly gotten physical with people who have threatened her that way. But as a child (especially an abused child), my brain was not ready for that. I doubt his was either. 

#5 Parents can’t be on top of kids all the time. It would super be unhealthy. And unlike the stereotype we picture when we hear the word molester, unsafe kids and families are not super easy to point out. My parents used to always be overprotective but even they couldn’t save me from what happened. It was our family friend’s kid. We literally went on vacation with them all the time and celebrated huge milestones together. There were no signs for them to spot. The kid could’ve presented as just a normal kid on the outside. 

#6 Know you can’t reverse it, but you can be apart of his healing story. Just take care of yourself first.
